title: An Ancient Technique
text: “If a race without the right aptitude tries to force its use, it won’t be good for the soul. Well, if someone with the right aptitude uses it, it’s quite effective. As they say, a little knowledge is a dangerous thing.”
“Even so, Rafumi-chan understands it, doesn’t she?”

“As a mechanism, yes. But to think such a technique existed… no, perhaps it existed from the very start. Strange that even the spirits of the Sacred Weapons kept silent about it. Or… perhaps it was simply lost, with no way left to pass it on.”
“What do you mean?”
“It means the reason the Heroes can’t use it is essentially the same as asking why they already are.”
I recall hearing something similar about ki once before, indeed.

“That technique works by entrusting one’s spirit-portion to another and having them wield it. The mechanism is extremely close to how a Hero’s weapon functions. No… perhaps it’s a method for amplifying power in those who haven’t yet reached the level of a spirit?”
“Hnn?”
“Rafumi, the way you explain it, only someone who already knows would understand, nano.”
“No, it means exactly what it sounds like. You understand what kind of existence I am, don’t you?”
“You’re chocolate, I say.”
“Hmph! As if.”
“Originally a spirit governing Valentine’s chocolate, nano… I see, so because it’s a spirit with a physical body, it understands.”
“That’s the gist of it.”

In a flash, Rafumi did to Rival exactly what the rabbit men had been trying to do earlier, I say. Something resembling Rafumi’s magic power seemed to flow into Rival. Rival then swiftly conjured something with magic—a pair of scissors, it seemed. Power took root in those scissors, forming something like a semi-transparent weapon. Snip, snip—Rival swung the scissors about.
“Match the wavelength.”
“N-nano… maintaining the breathing rhythm of cooperative magic while fighting sounds like it’ll take a lot of practice, nano.”
“There, now use a skill.”
“I know that, nano! Um, Air Strike Scissor Cut!”
Fwip! Rival unleashed something with the scissors that looked like a skill.
“And this one’s your—ah, no wonder you’re good with magic. Can you even cast without chanting?”
A dazzling flash of light—Rafumi conjured a magic circle, the kind Rival usually displayed when casting flashily, and sent it soaring into the sky.
“Understand now?”
“To some extent, nano.”
And with that, the reenactment between Rival and Rafumi came to a close.
“Seems like Gaelion-chan got it. Can you explain?”
“Give it a moment, nano. Gaelion understands the mechanism, but explaining it well is a bit tricky, nano. Not many races can even use this method, nano.”
“What kind of race are we talking about?”

“When a race that’s half-spirit cooperates and aligns their minds the way cooperative magic works, the spirit-half of that race possesses the other party, shares magic power, and both awaken their strength—that’s the technique, nano… The soul also joins in the substitute calculation, compensating for and strengthening whatever the race lacks, nano. Probably… it seems like it would also allow the corresponding race to take on a beast form. No, more accurately, entrusting the spirit-portion riding on the body eases the overload, nano.”
“Oh right, Rafumi-chan is also a spirit, isn’t she?”
“That’s right. That’s why I understand the mechanism. Well, there are different types of spirits too.”

Half-spirit, was it? For a moment I recalled a dream I once had alongside the spear’s spirit, about Mole rising in status by becoming a spirit, I say. If I remembered right, Rafumi had been there too, looking at me and laughing. Thinking of that, I glanced at Mole.

“So if someone without the aptitude—someone who isn’t a spirit—tries to use it, only the souls end up connected. That’s not a great method. It’s safer to simply align the magic power alone. Even while maintaining the chorus, the effect drops sharply, but a similar phenomenon occurs.”
“W-wait, don’t say scary things like that! I’ve already tried it as an experiment several times!”
“You’ll be fine. Though it seems there’s something distinctive about your body and soul.”
“That’s not something I can just let slide, is it?”
“Oh? Well, digging deeper might be interesting too… hehe.”
The moment Rafumi laughed, Rabbit Guy backed away.
“Please stop. I’d appreciate it if you didn’t do anything strange to me!”
“Half-spirit… wasn’t that true of the moles too?”
“Oh? So you remembered.”
The moment I muttered that, Itsuki, who had been sitting, stood up.
“What exactly is going on with the Rumo species?”
Of course—the Rumo species meant a great deal to Itsuki. No wonder he couldn’t let it pass.

“Ah, let me explain. It means they’re a race with the aptitude. They can master the technique discovered this time. Following the manner of cooperative magic, they entrust their spirit-portion to their partner, receive the partner’s magic power in return, and unleash the strength of their own body. It’s a race capable of turning breathing into power.”
“Wow… so this is where Imiya-chan and the others end up with a usable technique too. Theo seems to be able to use it too, oddly enough.”
“Just be careful. Compatibility matters.”
“Why is that?”

“The Sacred Weapons, the Seven Star Weapons too, they choose their wielder, don’t they? That’s compatibility. No matter how brave and valiant someone is, sometimes they simply can’t be chosen. That element is undoubtedly mixed in here as well. The reason the Heroes can’t do it is that the spirit is already aligned with them. The spirit’s output is simply too high for a living Rumo to match.”

Was there really such a troublesome mechanism at work? Had the spear’s spirit ever mentioned anything like that? Ah, but apparently there are candidates involved, so that must be why I was chosen. Among countless worlds, the spirit chooses whoever is most compatible and summons them as a Hero… is that how it works, I wonder?

“Right. This is just my guess, but Theodore, you should be able to use this technique with any of the Rumo species from the human side. Not just the Rumo species either—with any race that carries half a spirit within them. That’s the kind of form you have.”
“You mean I can use this technique with the Rumo folk? Not as the spirit side?”
“Well, if chosen, you’d likely be able to wield a weapon housing any spirit, and this time’s technique showed there’s a possibility you could draw out more output than other wielders.”
At Rafumi’s words, Rabbit Guy’s expression brightened a little, practically glowing with excitement. The look on his face screamed, “My time has finally come!”
“Theo looks kind of happy.”
“Well, it does feel a bit like being told I’m ‘the chosen one,’ so yeah, I guess I’m happy. Though having this person give me the stamp of approval feels a little iffy.”
“We get to be of use to everyone!”
The moles seemed quite intrigued by this.
“I want to try it.”
Mole too, it seemed.
“The issue comes down to compatibility, though, Rafumi-chan. Is there some kind of standard for that?”

“Further research might clarify it more, but as a rough guideline, it’s magical aptitude. Based on the Rumo species’ standard, they’d likely be most compatible with those who have an earth magic aptitude.”
“In that case, maybe Elmelo, among our group?”
“That would probably be the case.”
“We’ll look into this in every way we can! Let’s repay the Heroes’ kindness!”
“Yeahhh!”

And so, in this manner, a new technique was discovered, I say. In the end, when the power was properly combined, it seems the moles were able to transform further and increase their combat strength. Truly an ancient technique, it seemed. Word has it that Shieldfreeden decided to establish dedicated research into it going forward. It seems the aim is to break away from reliance on Takt. As an aside—shall I mention that Itsuki has been running wild all over Shieldfreeden in the meantime? His beloved moles, having gained a means to fight, are apparently working alongside Rabbit Guy, devoting themselves entirely to support roles. Itsuki certainly seemed to be in good spirits.
“Woof, this way, this way!”

And so, along with Father, we arrived at the mansion that was Wolf’s family home, I say. Yuki-chan and the others had been pulling the carriage the whole way there. The road had passed through a long stretch of forest. Deep in the mountains turned out to be a rather nice place, indeed.
“Yes, yes. I understand, but you don’t need to rush me so much. If anything, I’d appreciate it if you switched gears back to normal by now.”
“Very well then, Woof.”

At Father’s instruction, Wolf’s expression suddenly turned sharp and focused. Incidentally, Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy were with us, along with Panda and Elephant. Naturally, I had also brought Yuki-chan and the others along. None of the others had come this time. Rival and Rafumi were left behind to mind the house! Ha ha!
